deep.reconstruction:
This folio contains no computation. It is a note, in letter form, from Riemann to a collaborator he addresses with the familiar 'Du'. This is almost certainly Karl Hattendorff, who was working up Riemann's memoir 'Ueber die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalte bei gegebener Begrenzung', published posthumously in 1867. The note comments on Hattendorff's draft, which the previous page says was worked out 'heute Morgen'.

(1) Personal preamble. The main thing is that the work keeps moving. Hattendorff should not let Riemann's remarks hold him up. It is entirely up to him how far he adopts the changes.

(2) Methodological remark: two ways of regarding a surface.
(a) The surface as an infinitely thin body. This view is needed when surfaces are bent without stretching, as in the developing (Abwicklung) of one surface onto another. Gauss's investigations concern exactly the properties left unchanged by such bending: shortest lines (geodesics) and the measure of curvature (Gaussian curvature; Theorema Egregium). Riemann says his own 'Abwicklung der planities in das planum' also needs this view. This is probably an allusion to mapping or developing a two-dimensional manifold onto the plane, as in his own work, but the exact reference is uncertain.
(b) The view needed here. For the minimal-surface problem the bending-invariant view is not required. The opposition between the two sides of the surface (inner and outer) lies in the surface's relation to the surrounding space. That relation is exactly what view (a) abstracts away. So here the surface is treated as the boundary of a region of space, an 'Oberfläche'.

(3) Consequence for the method. For this problem it has long been found convenient to take as independent variables the quantities fixing the direction of the normal. Riemann cites Ossian Bonnet, Serret (reading uncertain) and Joachimsthal. In modern terms this means parametrising the surface by its Gauss map. On the adjacent pages this is done stereographically by a complex variable η and its conjugate η'. There 1/cos r = (1+ηη')/(1−ηη'), where r is the angle between the normal and the x-axis.

This requires fixing the side of the surface on which the normal counts as positive. My addition, not on the page: switching sides sends the normal n to −n, which in the stereographic variable is η → −1/η'. Under this map cos r = (1−ηη')/(1+ηη') changes sign, so the parametrisation genuinely depends on the choice of side.

(4) Editorial suggestion. Riemann suggests the distinction between the positive and negative side might later be motivated together with the introduction (or 'Einleitung') on the last sheet. He calls the change entirely inessential. He only wanted the occasion for a general conceptual remark about surfaces.

The next page continues with why the variables p, q are introduced. One reason is to allow imaginary independent variables. The other is to fix the orientation of boundary integrals once and for all through the antisymmetric symbol (∂f ∂g).
errors: No mathematical derivations on this page, hence no computational errors.
Conceptually sound. Orientability, i.e. a choice of normal side, is indeed extrinsic and irrelevant to Gauss's bending-invariant (intrinsic) geometry, while the Gauss-map parametrisation requires it.

results.what: Distinction between intrinsic (bending-invariant) properties of a surface, such as geodesics and Gaussian curvature, and extrinsic properties depending on the embedding in space, such as the two sides and the normal direction
results.modern_name: Intrinsic vs. extrinsic geometry; orientation / unit normal field
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas, 1827) for the intrinsic view; the distinction is standard

results.what: Using the normal direction (Gauss map) coordinates as independent variables for minimal surfaces, which requires fixing the positive side of the normal
results.modern_name: Gauss-map (stereographic normal) parametrisation of minimal surfaces; Weierstrass–Enneper-type representation
results.usually_credited_to: Ossian Bonnet (1850s), Joachimsthal, Serret; Riemann's 1867 posthumous memoir; Weierstrass and Enneper (1863–66)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an editorial and methodological note to Hattendorff on preparing the published minimal-surface memoir. It contains only a standard intrinsic/extrinsic remark, with an explicit attribution to Bonnet, Serret and Joachimsthal. It is of minor biographical and editorial interest only; the passing reference to his 'Abwicklung der planities in das planum' is a small curiosity.

checkable.asserts: With |η| = e, cos r = (1−ηη')/(1+ηη') and sin r = 2|η|/(1+ηη') satisfy cos²r + sin²r = 1, so η stereographically parametrises the unit normal.
With u = ηη', the side change η → −1/η' (u → 1/u) flips the sign of cos r, i.e. n → −n. Hence fixing the positive side is necessary.

transcription_corrections: Line 3: the image supports 'daß ich Dich dadurch bei der Ausarbeitung nicht zu binden[?] wünsche'. The verb remains uncertain.
'besteht wiederum in der Beziehung' may read 'besteht vielmehr in der Beziehung', which fits the sense better. Uncertain.
'in Verbindung mit der Einleitung der Unterscheidung' could also be 'Einführung'. Uncertain.
Name list: 'Ossian Bonnet, Serret[?], Joachimsthal' — 'Serret' is plausible but not certain from the image.
The struck word after 'Auffassung' in the second paragraph is illegible (crossed out) and is correctly marked as deletion.
